AC1 SATISFIED -- THE STALL IS OVER. AC2 patch applied to ~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh with operator approval, original backed up to rebar-dev-update.sh.pre-ac97.bak, and the updater run once to verify on the real thing rather than a harness.

Result:
  2026-09-04T05:06:47Z updated -> 6125c5345f0117d377acf72975c7c547316e537a (locked runtime; click override from uv.lock)
  2026-09-04T05:06:46Z prune summary: pruned=2 kept-live=0 remaining=4 (keep=3 cap=10)
  reject-streak: 122 -> 0
  current: releases/cdfd7d94d... (2026-08-28) -> releases/6125c5345f01... (current main)

So 122 consecutive failures and 201 commits of drift are ended, and the run also reclaimed two stale
release directories on its way through. Every session on this host now gets gate verdicts from
current code rather than a five-day-old build; the on-box MCP server is likewise no longer serving
stale gate code.

APPLICATION NOTE for whoever repeats this: 'git apply' REFUSES the diff because it names orig.sh /
new.sh -- it was generated from an extraction harness, not from a checkout. Use patch(1) against the
target explicitly: patch ~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh < <diff>. It applied cleanly, bash -n is
clean, and the hardcode at :18 is now UV_BIN="" with selection at :190.

WHY THIS FIX SHOULD NOT RE-INVERT, restated now that it is live: no absolute path is baked in.
PATH ORDER IS NO LONGER LOAD-BEARING -- every uv on PATH is probed by --version and the first exact
match wins, so neither Homebrew nor ~/.local/bin can shadow a satisfying binary in either direction.
The pin is read from the CANDIDATE COMMIT's own pyproject.toml after checkout, so it tracks main
rather than this host, which is the property the old hardcode lacked. REBAR_DEV_UV_BIN survives only
as a hint that is validated like any other candidate, never trusted.

STILL OPEN ON THIS TICKET:
 - AC4's detector is pushed for review as Gerrit change 2608 (not yet voted). Note it will now report
   CLEAN on this host, which is correct -- its live-host reading was already demoted to a one-time
   recorded datum (122 / 201 on 2026-09-03) precisely because AC1 destroys the observable condition.
   That AC-ordering fix has now paid off in practice rather than in theory.
 - AC5 (pruner 'Directory not empty' failures, and the 5fb693345b0c...1559 partial-release stub)
   remains open and untouched. Today's run pruned two releases successfully, so it is worth
   re-checking whether AC5 still reproduces before scoping work for it.
 - AC3 stays withdrawn per operator decision; AC4 absorbs its detection requirement.
